about: Every command an agent can call in Prism3: the MCP tools, the agent-link commands the Figma plugin answers, and the command-line entry points. Generated from the code; do not edit by hand.

tools.name: list_levers
tools.title: List brand controls
tools.description: List the complete BrandInput surface an agent can set: the lever catalog (grouped, labeled, typed, with enums, defaults and UI ranges — the same manifest the Figma plugin and web playground render from) PLUS the non-lever fields the manifest does not carry (identity, mode set, and the per-mode override layers). Call this first to learn what theme_brand accepts. Pass `describe` with field names to get those fields' full schema descriptions instead.

describe.description: BrandInput field names (e.g. ["typography", "radiusHairline"]). Returns each field's schema entry with every description in full, plus the $defs it references, instead of the catalog.

levers.description: The lever manifest — UI presentation contract.

nonLeverFields.description: BrandInput fields that are not UI knobs but are still accepted (and sometimes required).

required.description: Fields theme_brand will reject a call without.

described.description: With `describe`: { properties, $defs }, the named fields' full schema.

output.text: the same object as JSON in content[0].text

tools.name: theme_brand
tools.title: Generate a design-token system
tools.description: Generate a full design-token system from a brand input, and verify it. Returns the contrast-contract results (every declared a11y pair, computed on the resolved colors across all modes), alias integrity, and the decisions log by default. The DTCG token tree and the .ai.json agent metadata are OPT-IN via `include` because they are large — for a four-mode brand they measure roughly 890,000 and 590,000 characters respectively (~370,000 tokens combined). Arguments: { brand, include }. Call list_levers to see the controls, or validate_brand to check an input first. Each field description in the `brand` schema below is a one-line summary; list_levers with `describe` returns the full text.

brand.description: A BrandInput, the shape in packages/engine/schema/theme-schema.json, which tools/list sends compacted: each description cut to its one-line summary, every other keyword unchanged.

include.description: Sections to return, replacing the default ["notes"]. Add "tokens" and/or "aiMetadata" for the large payloads; pass [] for the verification result alone.

output.text: a JSON object in content[0].text; this tool declares no outputSchema

tools.name: score_consumption
tools.title: Score how an agent used the tokens
tools.description: Score generated output against a brand's token system — the check that closes the loop after theme_brand. Give it the token refs your output used and, optionally, the foreground/background pairs it put together. Returns: invented-token rate (refs naming tokens that do not exist), primitive-leak rate (refs reaching past the semantic layer into raw palette/dimension/font tiers), and contrast-contract compliance for every pair across every mode. Deterministic — no model judgment involved.

brand.description: The same BrandInput you passed to theme_brand — see that tool for the full input schema.

refs.description: Token refs the output used. Brace syntax, root-qualified or root-relative all accepted.

pairs.description: Optional foreground/background pairs the output placed together, checked against the contrast floor in EVERY mode.

kind.description: Sets the floor: text 4.5:1, large-text and ui 3:1. Defaults to text.

consumption.description: total / valid / invented / inventedRate / primitiveLeaks / primitiveLeakRate.

contracts.description: checked / pass / rate / failures / unresolved — omitted when no pairs were given.

output.text: the same object as JSON in content[0].text

tools.name: theme_from_brief
tools.title: Generate from a markdown brief
tools.description: Generate a token system from a design.md brief — YAML frontmatter plus prose — instead of a hand-assembled BrandInput. The natural entry point when working from a written brand description rather than known numbers: it parses the brief, reports the BrandInput it derived, and returns the same verification payload as theme_brand (with the same opt-in `include`). Call theme_brand directly when you already hold exact values.

brief.description: A design.md document. It must open with a --- YAML frontmatter fence on the first line.

include.description: Sections to return, replacing the default ["notes"]; same meaning as theme_brand.

output.text: a JSON object in content[0].text; this tool declares no outputSchema

tools.name: export_theme
tools.title: Write the token system to disk
tools.description: Generate a brand and WRITE its artifacts to a directory, returning a manifest of what was written — never the content. Use this instead of theme_brand include:["tokens"] whenever you want the actual files: the DTCG tree alone is roughly 890,000 characters for a four-mode brand, which no tool result should carry. Writes tokens.json (DTCG), ai-metadata.json, and a figma/ directory of Figma collection files. Arguments: { brand, outDir, include }. `outDir` must be a RELATIVE path. Requires a host that granted filesystem access; returns an error if not.

brand.description: The same BrandInput you would pass to theme_brand — see that tool for the full input schema.

outDir.description: Relative directory to write into (e.g. "./tokens"). Absolute paths and ".." segments are refused.

include.description: Artifact families to write. Defaults to all three.

output.text: the same object as JSON in content[0].text

tools.name: validate_brand
tools.title: Validate a brand input
tools.description: Validate a BrandInput against the engine schema and the engine's own input refusals, WITHOUT generating tokens. Returns { valid, errors } — a fast pre-flight before theme_brand. Takes the same brand object as theme_brand's `brand` argument; see that tool for the full input schema.

inputSchema.description: A BrandInput — the same shape as theme_brand's `brand` property.

output.text: the same object as JSON in content[0].text

mcp.transport: stdio, newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0; drives the running plugin over a WebSocket on 127.0.0.1:17331

tools.name: figma_status
tools.description: Whether the Prism3 plugin in the owner's Figma is connected to this bridge, the link state it last reported, and any command in flight. Call first. For the file's own state, run the `status` command with figma_run.

output.text: a JSON object in content[0].text; this tool declares no outputSchema

tools.name: figma_run
tools.description: Run one agent-link command in the connected plugin and return its result envelope (v, id, cmd, ok, startedAt, finishedAt, engineVersion, transport, result {verdict, data, logs} | error, progress). Commands: status, apply-theme, build-components, file-setup, style-guide, prune, readback, update-components, capture-baseline, adopt-members. The plugin runs it through the same handler the panel's button reaches. 'prune' with confirm: true deletes — preview with confirm: false first.

args.description: apply-theme: {input: BrandInput}; build-components: {def?}; prune: {input, confirm}; others: {}

timeoutMs.description: Default 600000 (a full catalog build takes minutes).

output.text: a JSON object in content[0].text; this tool declares no outputSchema

tools.name: figma_logs
tools.description: Console and progress lines the plugin streamed, newest last. Pass `since` (the `last` from a previous call) to read only new lines.

output.text: a JSON object in content[0].text; this tool declares no outputSchema

agentLink.precondition: The owner has switched the agent link on in the plugin, in the file the agent is working in.

command.id: 1 to 64 characters of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, dot, underscore or hyphen

result.shape: { v, id, cmd, ok, startedAt, finishedAt, engineVersion, transport, result: { verdict, data, logs } | error: { code, message }, progress? }

mailbox.about: The file's root shared plugin data, for an agent whose only Figma access is a use_figma call. The agent writes the inbox; the plugin writes everything else.

bridge.about: A local WebSocket the plugin panel connects to, driven through the figma-bridge MCP server's figma_run tool.

errors.meaning: Not an object, or `id`/`issuedAt` missing or unusable.
`args` is not the shape that cmd takes.
The command was already queued when the owner switched the link on, so it was not run.
The handler threw past its own catch — a defect in the plugin, reported rather than swallowed.
A bridge command reached the plugin after the owner switched the link off.
A run of the same write was already going, the panel's or an agent's, so this one was not run (#1957).

commands.name: status
commands.description: Engine version, plugin build, the file's themed state, and which transports are listening.
commands.writes: Nothing. Reads the link state, the plugin build and the file's themed state.

commands.name: apply-theme
commands.description: A full `BrandInput`, as the UI's Apply sends it.
commands.writes: Variables, collections, text styles and effect styles for the brand, as the panel's Apply does.

refuses.message: apply-theme needs args.input: a BrandInput object, as the UI's Apply sends it

commands.name: build-components
commands.description: A `componentDefs` id; absent means Button, as for the UI message.
commands.writes: Component sets on their component pages, creating a page when it is missing.

refuses.message: build-components takes args.def: a component def id, or no def for Button

commands.name: file-setup
commands.description: The page scaffold + the two template assets. No payload.
commands.writes: The page structure (cover, dividers, section pages) and the two template assets. Idempotent.

commands.name: style-guide
commands.description: The color style-guide tables (#259) — every field optional, as the panel's Customize options.

refuses.message: style-guide takes args.collections: an array of collection names
style-guide takes args.types: an array of token types, e.g. ['color']
style-guide takes args.valueFormat: hex, rgba, hsl or hsb
style-guide takes args.header: dark or light
style-guide takes args.display: auto, default, text, icon, border or transparency
style-guide takes args.aliases and args.description as booleans
style-guide takes args.dimensionDisplay: filled or line (auto means filled)
style-guide takes args.fontDisplay: auto, generic, family, size, weight, letterSpacing or lineHeight
style-guide takes args.rem, args.paragraphSpacing and args.textDecoration as booleans
style-guide takes args.titleCell as a boolean
style-guide takes args.tokenNames: full (the whole variable name) or short (the name below the table's shared prefix)
style-guide takes args.tables: a non-empty array of table titles or keys, e.g. ['Primary — prism']

commands.name: prune
commands.description: `confirm: false` previews, `confirm: true` deletes — the UI's two-step prune, in one field.
commands.writes: With confirm: false, nothing (a preview of what would go). With confirm: true, deletes the variables and styles the brand no longer emits, recomputed from a fresh read.

refuses.message: prune needs args.input: a BrandInput object
prune needs args.confirm: false to preview, true to delete

commands.name: readback
commands.description: The boot read-back (`seed-info`) plus a census of every component page. Read-only.
commands.writes: Nothing. Reads the file's themed state and a census of every component page.

commands.name: update-components
commands.args: { def?: string; confirm: false } | { def?: string; confirm: true; previewHash: string; choices?: UpdateChoiceArgs }
commands.description: #2265: the in-place update. `confirm: false` (or absent) checks and writes nothing, and its result carries a `previewHash`; `confirm: true` applies the update that check described, and must echo that `previewHash` (PR 2). The plugin reads the file again and refuses when it no longer hashes the same. No `def` means every def that projects a set.
commands.writes: With confirm: false (or none), nothing: a check whose result carries a previewHash. With confirm: true and that previewHash, updates the sets in place; refused when the file no longer hashes the same.

refuses.message: update-components takes args.def: a component def id, or no def for every set
update-components takes args.confirm: false (or none) to check, true to apply
update-components with confirm: true needs args.previewHash: the previewHash its check returned

commands.name: capture-baseline
commands.description: #2265: record the as-built baseline on members built before it existed. No `def` means every set.
commands.writes: Plugin data only: the as-built record on members built before it existed.

refuses.message: capture-baseline takes args.def: a component def id, or no def for every set

commands.name: adopt-members
commands.description: #2283: the one-time Adopt (§10 Q4). Records and stamps members Prism3 did not build, so an update can bring them to the plan in place. No `def` means every set.
commands.writes: Plugin data only: records and stamps members Prism3 did not build, so an update can bring them to the plan.

refuses.message: adopt-members takes args.def: a component def id, or no def for every set

commands.name: run-code
commands.description: #2530, dev builds only: the body of an async function to run in the main thread (`dev-commands.ts`).
commands.writes: Whatever the code writes. Dev builds only; a release build answers unknown-command.

refuses.message: run-code needs args.code: the body of an async function, as a string
run-code takes args.timeoutMs: milliseconds from 1 to ${MAX_TIMEOUT_MS}

cli.summary: Prism3 engine — CLI adapter (the authoring on-ramp; docs/07 §6 + §11).

usage.text: npx tsx packages/engine/cli.ts <design.md> [--out <dir>] [--fidelity]

cli.summary: Prism3 engine — MCP adapter (docs/08 §5, roadmap C: "an agent themes Prism3").

usage.text: npx tsx packages/engine/mcp.ts

cli.summary: regen.ts — the single entry point for regenerating EVERY committed generated artifact — `out/**`, the three emitted `schema/` contracts, and the two engine-root reports, and the analysis reports under `docs/public/reports/` (#2651) — plus the drift gate that proves the committed copies still match what the engine emits (#281).

usage.text: npx tsx packages/engine/regen.ts            # regenerate everything, in place
npx tsx packages/engine/regen.ts --check    # fail (exit 1) if the committed artifacts have drifted

cli.summary: Prism3 engine — TOKEN CONTRACT (the corpus build + the breaking-change gate).

usage.text: npx tsx packages/engine/token-contract.ts --check    # fail (exit 1) if the surface moved
npx tsx packages/engine/token-contract.ts --accept   # rewrite the baseline (requires the bump)

cli.summary: Prism3 engine — MATERIALISE-TO-FIGMA (the round-trip payload generator).

usage.text: npx tsx packages/engine/materialise-to-figma.ts <brand>            # manifest: passes + byte sizes
npx tsx packages/engine/materialise-to-figma.ts <brand> --pass palette
npx tsx packages/engine/materialise-to-figma.ts <brand> --pass color-create
npx tsx packages/engine/materialise-to-figma.ts <brand> --pass color-aliases
npx tsx packages/engine/materialise-to-figma.ts <brand> --pass verify
npx tsx fold.ts             # fold everything pending, then regen
npx tsx fold.ts --dry-run   # print the plan, write nothing
npx tsx packages/engine/visualize.ts               # writes out/tokens.html too
npx tsx packages/engine/visualize.ts --out <dir>   # writes <dir>/tokens.html instead
npx tsx verify.ts            # every gate, in order, with a PASS/FAIL table
npx tsx verify.ts --list     # the authored list, run nothing

cli.summary: figma-bridge — the agent link's TRANSPORT B: a local MCP server that drives the RUNNING Prism3 plugin in the owner's Figma desktop app over a localhost WebSocket.

usage.text: npx tsx tools/figma-bridge/server.ts [--port 17331]      (or PRISM3_BRIDGE_PORT)

cli.summary: agent-link — print the short `use_figma` script that sends a command to the RUNNING Prism3 plugin through the file, or reads its result back.

usage.text: npx tsx tools/figma-mcp/agent-link.ts send <cmd> [<args.json> | '<json>'] [--brand <id|path>] [--id <id>]
npx tsx tools/figma-mcp/agent-link.ts read <id> [--path result.data.apply.misses]
npx tsx tools/figma-mcp/agent-link.ts link

cli.summary: `plan.ts` — write the numbered `use_figma` scripts for one brand, plus a manifest (#111 / #1553).

usage.text: npx tsx tools/figma-mcp/plan.ts --brand <file.design.md | example id> [--apply] [--build all|<id>,<id>]

cli.summary: `report.ts` — turn a run's returned JSON into one pass/fail summary (#111 / #1553).

usage.text: npx tsx tools/figma-mcp/report.ts --manifest <out>/manifest.json --results <out>/results

cli.summary: Prism3 — THE AGENT REFERENCE (#2637, owner Q300 A).

usage.text: npx tsx packages/engine/emit-agent-reference.ts            # write the reference
npx tsx packages/engine/emit-agent-reference.ts --check    # fail (exit 1) if it no longer matches the code

cli.summary: Prism3 — THE FIGMA CONVENTIONS FILE (#2647, owner Q306.2 A).

usage.text: npx tsx packages/engine/emit-figma-conventions.ts            # write the conventions file
npx tsx packages/engine/emit-figma-conventions.ts --check    # fail (exit 1) if it no longer matches the code
